model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the “effect” (y-axis, ranging from 0 to 30 with major ticks at intervals of 10) of six different language models — mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂ — across nine language families or categories on the x-axis: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. Each category displays six grouped bars, color-coded and labeled in the legend: light blue (mBERT-L₂), medium blue (XLM-L₂), light green (mBERT-R₂), dark green (XLM-R₂), light pink (mBERT-B₂), and red (XLM-B₂). Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. The IE-Indic group shows the highest effects, particularly for mBERT-R₂ (~20), XLM-R₂ (~18), mBERT-B₂ (~24), and XLM-B₂ (~21). The Semitic group also exhibits high values for mBERT-L₂ (~11), XLM-L₂ (~16), and XLM-B₂ (~20). In contrast, Isolate and Uralic show consistently low effects across all models, mostly near zero. The IE-Slavic family shows moderate effects, especially for mBERT-B₂ (~17) and XLM-B₂ (~15). Most bars are unsorted within groups, and no single model consistently outperforms others across all language families.
